chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan said: 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr narrated to us from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr al-Ahwal from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:'

The Tashahhud in the first two Rak'ahs is: 'All praise is for Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and accept his intercession for his nation and raise his rank.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The Taslim (salutation of peace) in prayer is of four types: If the man is an Imam, he gives one Taslim; if he is a Ma'mum (follower) and there is no one to his left, he gives one Taslim as well; if there is a person to his left, he gives two Taslims; and if he is alone, he gives one Taslim. What indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.اَلتَّشَهُّدُ: Tashahhud (testimony of faith recited in prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct text for Tashahhud and how many times should one say Taslim in prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* provides the precise liturgical formula for the Tashahhud, emphasizing the dual testimony of God's oneness and Muhammad's prophethood, followed by specific supplications for the Prophet's intercession and elevated status. It further elucidates the jurisprudential nuances of the Taslim (salutation), distinguishing between the single or double salutations required based on the pray-er's role (Imam or Ma'mum) and the presence of a companion to the left, reflecting the practical application of ritual purity and communal prayer dynamics in Shia fiqh.
